# Instructions for accurately reporting failed municipal water-quality tests to protect the public

source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately reporting failed municipal water-quality tests to protect the public

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Verify test results for accuracy.
3. Identify failing parameters that exceed regulatory limits.
4. Note the date and time of the sampling.
5. Detail the location of the failed test, specifying the sampling point.

6. Classify the type of contamination detected (e.g., coliform bacteria, lead, turbidity).
7. Specify the concentration levels and how they compare to the regulatory standard.
8. Consult with laboratory staff or water-quality experts for an interpretation of test results.

9. Document any previous failures at the same location or within the municipal water system.
10. Establish the frequency of the testing and whether the failure is part of a trend.
11. Indicate the possible causes of the water-quality failure.
12. Describe any immediate remedial actions taken by the municipality.

13. Communicate the failure to the regulatory agency responsible for water quality oversight.
14. Initiate a public notification process if required by regulations or if there is a direct threat
